ground.name: Drift sargassum
ground.source: underwater — Sargassum fluitans, second holopelagic species forming Atlantic and Caribbean windrows, 0.2-1 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Sargassum fluitans, second holopelagic species forming Atlantic and Caribbean windrows, 0
traits.leaf_shape: strap or rosette leaves in a clump on a branch
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: serrate leaf-like blades with round bladders, drawn as small leaves

ground.silhouette: floating golden-brown tangle with berry floats

growth.juvenile_note: No seedlings: it floats all its life, never attaches and has no known sexual stage; new plants are fragments that break off and keep growing (days here = a fragment resuming growth). A young clump is a small floating tangle of golden-brown, finely thorny stems with broad (3-6 mm) toothed blades and smooth, round, pea-sized air bladders on short stalks.
growth.source: Parr 1939 and later Sargasso Sea work (holopelagic, reproduces only by fragmentation); Lapointe 1995 Limnol Oceanogr (pelagic Sargassum doubles in ~11 days in nutrient-rich coastal water, much slower offshore); Schell et al. 2015 (S. fluitans vs S. natans morphology); clump age estimated

ground.name: Pelagic sargassum
ground.source: underwater — Sargassum natans, free-floating holopelagic brown alga of the Sargasso Sea and tropical Atlantic gyre, surface rafts 0.2-1 m thick — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Sargassum natans, free-floating holopelagic brown alga of the Sargasso Sea and tropical Atlantic gyre, surf
traits.leaf_shape: strap or rosette leaves in a clump on a branch
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: narrow toothed blades, bladders spine-tipped; drawn as small leaves

ground.silhouette: floating golden-brown tangle with berry floats

growth.juvenile_note: No seedlings: it floats all its life with no known sexual stage; new plants are fragments that break off and keep growing (days here = a fragment resuming growth). A young clump is a bushy floating tangle of smooth golden-brown stems with long, very narrow (1-3 mm) toothed blades and round air bladders, each tipped with a small spine.
growth.source: Parr 1939 and Wikipedia Sargassum natans (holopelagic, reproduces by fragmentation); Lapointe 1995 Limnol Oceanogr (doubling in ~11 days in nutrient-rich water, slower in the open Sargasso Sea); Schell et al. 2015 (narrow blades and spine-tipped bladders distinguish S. natans); clump age estimated
